headline: タオル, “(hand) towel”, is the English word “towel” in katakana.
取り出す is 取る (toru, “to take”) plus 出す (dasu, “to put out”).
スポーツ, “sport(s)”, is borrowed from the English plural “sports”.
量, “quantity, amount”, comes from Middle Chinese 量 (MC ljangH, “measure”).
タイトル is borrowed from English “title”.
スタンド is borrowed from English “stand” and first attested in 1902.
野, “field”, is from Old Japanese, written ⟨no₁⟩ in the source.
ウーマン is the English word “woman” in katakana.
殺す, “to kill”, is from Old Japanese and first attested in the Nihon Shoki of 720 CE.
ソフト covers “soft”, a soft hat and software, and the source traces it to English “soft”.
もし, “if”, is from Old Japanese and attested in the Man'yōshū of 759.
パスポート is borrowed from English “passport”.
旗, “flag”, is from Old Japanese, from Proto-Japonic *pata.
ラケット is the English word “racket” in katakana.
ハンドル covers “handle” and “steering wheel”, and the source traces it to English “handle”.
生年月日, “birth date”, is 生 (“birth”) plus 年 (“year”) plus 月 (“month”) plus 日 (“day”).
ギター is borrowed from English “guitar”.
買い物, “shopping”, is 買い (kai) plus 物 (-mono).
ダイヤモンド is borrowed from English “diamond”.
針, “needle”, began as pari in Old Japanese, and its p reached h by way of ɸ.
ドラマ is borrowed from English “drama” and first cited to 1879.
めまい, “dizziness”, is likely a compound of 目 (me, “eye”) plus 舞い (mai), from the verb “to dance; to rotate”.
ワイン is borrowed from English “wine”.
スイッチ is borrowed from English “switch”.
いつでも is glossed literally as “at even any time”.
ショップ is borrowed from English “shop”.
棚, “shelves, rack”, was written with the phonetic man'yōgana 多奈 in the Nihon Shoki of 720 CE.
コース is borrowed from English “course”.
扇ぐ is inherited from Old Japanese, and the source calls the shift from apu to ao irregular.
デート is the English “date”, in the sense of a social engagement.
